articles.title: Dolph Ziggler net worth 2026: How Nic Nemeth built his wrestling fortune, inside his WWE and acting career and more
articles.summary: Dolph Ziggler, now known as Nic Nemeth, is an American professional wrestler, comedian, and actor.
articles.body: Dolph Ziggler, now known as Nic Nemeth, is an American professional wrestler, comedian, and actor. He spent nearly two decades with WWE before leaving the company in 2023. Since then, he has continued his wrestling career with TNA Wrestling, New Japan Pro-Wrestling, AAA, and independent promotions.His journey includes multiple world titles, memorable WWE moments, and success outside the company. He was popular as "The Showoff". He built a reputation for his athletic ability and in-ring performances.Dolph Ziggler net worth in 2026Dolph Ziggler has an estimated net worth of $4 million (as per Celebrity Net Worth). His wealth comes from his long WWE career, championship success, independent wrestling appearances, comedy shows, acting projects, and merchandise.Nemeth spent 19 years with WWE after signing with the company in 2004. His earnings included contract payments, bonuses, merchandise royalties, and live-event appearances. A 2015 report from Celebrity Net Worth estimated his annual compensation at around $900,000, including travel and accommodation. A later 2018 report from Sports Illustrated claimed he had agreed to a deal worth approximately $1.5 million annually. However, Nemeth disputed that specific report. Born Nicholas Theodore Nemeth on July 27, 1980, in Cleveland, Ohio, he developed an interest in wrestling as a child. He attended St. Edward High School in Lakewood, Ohio, where he excelled in amateur wrestling.Nemeth continued wrestling at Kent State University. He won three Mid-American Conference championships and recorded 121 career victories. He also studied political science and had a pre-law minor. Before joining WWE, he had been accepted into law school at Arizona State University. He signed with WWE in 2004 and began training in Ohio Valley Wrestling. His first major television role came in 2006 as Nicky, a member of the Spirit Squad. After returning to developmental wrestling, he adopted the Dolph Ziggler name in 2008.Ziggler became one of WWE’s most decorated performers. He won the World Heavyweight Championship twice, the Intercontinental Championship six times, and the United States Championship twice. He also captured several tag team titles and the NXT Championship. One of his biggest moments came in April 2013. Ziggler cashed in his Money in the Bank contract against Alberto Del Rio on the night after WrestleMania 29. He won the World Heavyweight Championship as the crowd erupted. Another memorable performance came at Survivor Series in 2014. Ziggler became the sole survivor for Team Cena.In 2022, he won the NXT Championship by defeating Bron Breakker and Tommaso Ciampa in a triple-threat match. WWE released him in September 2023, ending his long run with the company.After leaving WWE, Nemeth began performing under his real name. He found success in other promotions.Nemeth has also pursued stand-up comedy throughout his wrestling career. He has performed at comedy clubs and toured with his own shows. His acting credits include the WWE Studios film Countdown and the comedy Me Him Her. articles.title: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s Week 7 game vs Charleston Southern
articles.summary: Here’s a look at what we’re thinking for Clemson’s post bye week matchup against Charleston Southern.
articles.body:
Clemson has had an extra week to address its problems. Saturday offers the first look at whether that time produced meaningful progress.

The Tigers welcome Charleston Southern to Memorial Stadium for a noon ET kickoff on ACC Network, looking to build some momentum before returning to conference play. At 3-2 overall, Clemson still has plenty to accomplish, but its latest loss left Dabo Swinney's team with considerable work ahead.

Pass protection will be among the biggest areas to watch. Miami repeatedly disrupted Clemson's offense in its 41-13 victory, recording six sacks and nine tackles for loss. Giving freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds more room to operate would be an encouraging starting point coming out of the open date.

There were productive moments through the air despite that pressure. Reynolds finished with a season-high 295 passing yards, while Bryant Wesco Jr. delivered nine catches for 152 yards. Clemson will look to turn those individual performances into a more consistent offensive showing.

Charleston Southern arrives at 3-3 after beating South Carolina State 49-39, with quarterback Jared Echols throwing three touchdown passes in the win.

For Clemson, the question extends beyond whether it can get back into the win column. How convincingly can the Tigers take control, and what will their performance reveal about the weeks ahead?

Here is how our staff sees Saturday's matchup playing out.

Alex Turri: Clemson 42, Charleston Southern 9

Clemson coming off the bye week should be a good thing for the Tigers. Tait Reynolds gets some time to figure out his game a little mkre and the offensive line hopefully figures out a way to at least be passable. The defense is no concern.

The reason I say should, however, is how many letdowns we've seen from the Tigers coming off of some free time. Expectations high, downfall comes in a shocking fashion. Just feels like a recent trend. That being said, Clemson is way better and going to dominate.

Steve Holley: Clemson 45, Charleston Southern 6

Tait Reynolds showed some promise in the loss to Miami. This is a chance for him and others to gain some confidence once ACC play resumes next week against Virginia Tech. Reynolds, Gideon Davidson and the rest of the offense has a big game and Clemson heads into the second half of its season 4-2.

articles.title: Browns RB Quinshon Judkins gets glimmer of hope in latest injury update
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins took a positive step in his recovery from a foot injury by returning to practice Friday ahead of the team’s We...
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins took a positive step in his recovery from a foot injury by returning to practice Friday ahead of the team's Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens . However, his availability for Sunday's AFC North contest remains uncertain, as he is listed as questionable.

Judkins sustained the injury during the Browns' Week 5 loss to the New York Jets . He missed Wednesday's practice and returned Thursday as a limited participant, attending the session but sitting out team stretching and individual drills.

The 22-year-old has recorded 221 rushing yards and one touchdown on 73 carries through five games, averaging 3.0 yards per attempt. He has also contributed 18 receptions for 102 yards. If he is cleared to play but remains limited by the injury, Cleveland could reduce his workload.

If Judkins cannot play or is unable to handle his usual responsibilities, Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime could receive increased opportunities. Estime recently joined Cleveland after spending time on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad.

Judkins was among four Browns players who returned to practice Friday, alongside Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Derek Barnett.

articles.title: Detroit Lions place trio on injured reserve
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions announced that Ben Bartch, Tom Kennedy, and Devin White have been placed on injured reserve.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions announced roster moves on Friday, placing three players on injured reserve.

Offensive guard Ben Bartch, linebacker Devin White, and wide receiver and return man Tom Kennedy were all placed on injured reserve. By rule, all three must now miss at least four games before they would be eligible to return to play.

Kennedy suffered an MCL injury that requires surgery last Sunday in Detroit's 45-21 win at the Arizona Cardinals . Dan Campbell and the Lions were initially hopeful that Kennedy's injury wouldn't be a long-term concern, but further testing showed otherwise.

"It was significant enough where he'll be out for the season. That's the stinker right there," Campbell said of Kennedy on Monday.

The 5-foot-10, 195-pound receiver and return man had handled all of the Lions ' punt return duties prior to his injury, returning six punts for 79 yards. Kennedy's 13.2 yards per punt return ranked sixth in the NFL. Kennedy also averaged 24.9 yards per kickoff return on 10 attempts thus far this season.

White suffered a broken forearm against Arizona that Campbell said requires surgery. Detroit expects White back at some point this season, though.

"We'll get him back at some point. It'll just be a while," Campbell said of White.

Per Pro Football Focus , White has logged 67 defensive snaps this season, totaling 10 tackles in three starts.

Lastly, Bartch was inactive in Week 5 with a foot injury. The 6-foot-6, 318-pound lineman took over for Christian Mahogany at left guard in the Lions' opener after Mahogany went down with injury.

Bartch would total 66 snaps in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints , and then he started in Week 2 at the Buffalo Bills before Mahogany made his return from a hip injury against the New York Jets in Week 3.

With these moves, the Lions have three open roster spots. It paves the way for returns to the active roster for both safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays.

articles.title: Report: Oregon expected to start Brock Thomas at QB vs. Nebraska
articles.summary: Oregon is expected to start third-string QB Brock Thomas on Saturday against Nebraska, per reports.
articles.body:
The revenge matchup between Dylan Raiola and Nebraska will have to wait. After stepping in and nearly leading the Oregon Ducks' offense to a fourth-quarter comeback last week against UCLA, the Ducks are moving forward with third-string quarterback Brock Thomas as the starter on Saturday night against the Cornhuskers . CBS Sports' Chris Hummer and Matt Zenitz first reported the news.

With Dante Moore remaining on the sideline while he recovers from a concussion, Thomas will make his first start as a senior with his hometown team, having graduated from Sheldon High School, which also produced Justin Herbert . Thomas played well in the fourth quarter last week against UCLA, completing 11-of-16 passes for 156 yards and one touchdown.

Thomas also stepped in last season for Moore at home against Wisconsin. Although the conditions were rainy and less than ideal, Thomas completed all four of his pass attempts in the second half to win, 21-7. He led two drives that both lasted nearly six minutes and kept the ball out of harm's way, which is likely what he will be tasked with replicating against Nebraska's aggressive defense .

It was almost unfathomable that Raiola wouldn't start this game a week ago. After turning in a superb performance off the bench on the road at USC, throwing for nearly 300 yards and two touchdowns, Raiola cratered last week in his first Oregon start.

The former five-star was benched at the end of the third quarter against the Bruins after completing just six of his 19 pass attempts and turning the ball over three times.

By turning to Thomas, the Ducks are prioritizing clean play on offense, although Raiola might have a better chance to put up points. Oregon will lean on its defensive game plan to stop the Cornhuskers and play keepaway with the ball. Evan Stewart , Oregon's leading receiver this season, is listed as doubtful to play, so Thomas will have one less weapon to work with.

articles.title: Good Sports: Bulldog Blitz descending back into the Valley
articles.summary: Some traditions are just too good to stay grounded as a Valley skydiving team is making its way to high school football games.
articles.body:
A skydiving team with deep ties to Valley football communities is continuing a tradition of delivering game balls and entertaining fans before kickoff, while creating lasting memories for its members.

Most schools require patrons to enter through the front gate on Friday nights. But at a recent game between Kerman and Kingsburg, members of the Bulldog Blitz skydiving team arrived from above.

"This was the first year Kerman invited us to come skydive. So it was pretty amazing," said Brandy Robertson, a Kerman teacher and skydiver with Bulldog Blitz.

Robertson delivered the game ball to a roaring crowd at the home of the Lions. The experience also brought personal connections.

"When I landed, I actually had some students from the past... and they came up and gave me a hug and, you know, said, Oh, Ms. Robertson! How are you?" Robertson said.

The excitement generated by the jumps is not limited to one school. Members of the team also descend into Valley Children's Stadium on game days, where fans have embraced the tradition.

"I like the crank turns into the stadium and the roar of the crowd is something that's exhilarating," said Kingsburg alumnus Luke Breshears, who has been skydiving for 10 years.

The Bulldog Blitz skydiving team brought skydiving back to Bulldog football games in 2015.

"To see that fan base and hear that roar. It's a true passion to give back to the community," said Chris Boling, co-founder of Bulldog Blitz Skydiving.

For some team members, the tradition spans generations.

"In my case, it was my dad that was skydiving into the games. So it was always, you know, this kind of legendary goal to aspire to. But that's one of the things that I hold the closest near and dear to my heart," said Sarah Gilbert, a Madera alumna who has been skydiving for 20 years.

Robertson said she grew up watching members of the team perform the same jumps she now takes part in.

"Those were actually the guys that were skydiving on the field when I was a child... this thing that you never think that you'll be able to do. And it was really like the best feeling," she said.

Beyond the game-day spectacle, team members say the experience has helped create lifelong bonds. From marriage proposals on Jim Sweeney's field to relationships formed through the sport, they describe Bulldog Blitz as more than a skydiving team.

"We've been doing this for so long and we love and care for each other so deeply. And this experience has been something that is going to be in our life forever," said MaryAnn Boling, co-founder of Bulldog Blitz Skydiving.

articles.title: 'A relief that it was over': China No.1 Wei Yi, now Chess Olympiad gold medallist, reveals taking 'long break' after Candidates
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The last game of Wei Yi's first Candidates Tournament lasted 32 moves.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The last game of Wei Yi's first Candidates Tournament lasted 32 moves. Javokhir Sindarov had already clinched the title and the right to challenge India's Dommaraju Gukesh in the upcoming World Championship match; Wei Yi had nothing left to chase. And subsequently, neither player pressed for a win, and the game ended in a draw after roughly ten minutes.China's Wei Yi, who more recently clinched an individual gold on Board 2 in the open section of the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, does not dress things up when you ask the Chinese No. 1 how he felt when his first Candidates Tournament ended in Cyprus. There is no talk of glory or regret."My first feeling was that I was extremely tired," the Grandmaster told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "I remember taking a long rest after the final round. It was a relief that the tournament was finally over."For a game that involves little physical activity, with players seated across a board and moving pieces, the admission might seem unusual to some. But the remark points to something the sport rarely acknowledges openly.At the highest level, the game of 64 squares is far from a comfortable place to be."It was my first Candidates Tournament, and playing 14 classical games in such an intense atmosphere, against opponents of such a high standard, was certainly not easy," he added.Fourteen games, ten drawsOn paper, the 2758-rated Grandmaster had a steady rather than spectacular debut in Cyprus, including two wins, two losses, ten draws, 7/14, and a fourth-place finish.Sindarov finished on 10, Anish Giri on 8.5, and Fabiano Caruana on 7.5. Wei Yi finished ahead of Hikaru Nakamura (6.5) and Praggnanandhaa (6).He had earned his seat by beating Andrey Esipenko in the Goa World Cup semi-final, and he opened with draws against fellow debutant Matthias Bluebaum and Praggnanandhaa.The damage came in rounds three and six. Caruana beat him in 19 moves, the game he singles out. Sindarov, playing him in classical for the first time, won a queen-and-rook endgame under time pressure, his fourth straight victory on the way to a runaway finish.Both of Wei Yi's wins came against Esipenko, in rounds seven and 13. In the second, a sharp Petroff, he admitted he had been lucky to survive the opening."Looking back, I'm not particularly satisfied with my overall performance," he explained. "I think I could have played better in several games, especially my game against Fabiano Caruana, possibly the one from the third round.""That said, I was also somewhat fortunate during the tournament. In at least three games, my position became very difficult after the first time control. My opponents were probably tired as well, and they made some mistakes during the second time control."Those were his draws against Nakamura, Praggnanandhaa and Giri. Fatigue, in other words, cuts both ways.Why players step awayFew know that toll better than his countryman Ding Liren. Ding became China's first undisputed world champion in April 2023. After a poor showing in Romania that May, he took nine months away from tournaments, citing a struggle with depression. He lost the title to India's Gukesh in December 2024, then played no classical games in 2025. In April this year, he resurfaced at the Chinese Team Championship and scored 4/5.Speaking to this website on the sidelines of the Global Chess League in Bengaluru, where he was playing for Triveni Continental Kings, Wei Yi assessed the overall situation with Liren."I think the circumstances behind our respective breaks were somewhat different," Wei, who also took a break due to his studies some years ago, added."I went to university, and the COVID-19 pandemic happened to begin around the same time. I felt it was a good opportunity because there weren't many tournaments taking place," he continued. "But I continued participating in major events, such as the Grand Prix.""Regardless of who it is, I understand why a player might want to take some time off to rest and regain their form," he shared. "As a professional chess player myself, I know the pressure players face during tournaments. The pressure can be enormous, especially when you reach the highest level."'Hope chess becomes as famous in China as it is in India'Wei Yi has been visiting India since 2014, when he played the World Youth Championship in Pune."I've visited India many times, so many that I've probably lost count," he said with a smile. "Since then, I've also visited Hyderabad, Goa, Mumbai and Kolkata. When I list them all, I've actually been to quite a few Indian cities."I think all the cities I've visited have been very nice, and the organisers of the tournaments I've attended have generally done an excellent job. The atmosphere in the Indian countryside has left a particularly deep impression on me."When it comes to chess, the 1999-born, has just one wish, as he concluded, "Personally, I think Indian chess has developed rapidly over the past few years, and that is something people around the world can see. I would like to see chess receive more support in China so that it can become as popular there as it is in India."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NCAA moves to block Ohio Governor Mike DeWine's executive order expanding college athletes' eligibility
articles.summary: The NCAA filed a federal lawsuit against Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine, claiming his executive order gives Ohio schools an unfair competitive advantage.
articles.body: The NCAA filed a lawsuit against Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine on Friday, escalating a dispute that began three days earlier when he signed an executive order giving state universities the option to allow athletes who graduated from high school in 2022 to compete for a fifth college season. The order challenges a new NCAA eligibility rule that excludes those athletes. The suit was filed in federal court in Ohio. NCAA President Charlie Baker described taking the legal action as an "extraordinary step" intended to prevent DeWine from making it "impossible for all schools to compete on a level playing field." In the lawsuit, the NCAA accused DeWine, a two-term Republican governor, of trying to give Ohio athletes "a hall pass" from following NCAA rules. NCAA WINS TENTH CIRCUIT 'STAY', BUT FACES MORE ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FROM 2022 CLASS ATHLETES IN CHAOTIC TIME DeWine’s executive order and the NCAA’s lawsuit in response mark the latest escalation in a wave of legal maneuvering that is reshaping college sports rules on a state-by-state basis. The latest clash quickly prompted reactions from across the college athletics landscape. "This whole thing has become comical," University of Tennessee athletic director Danny White said on social media in reaction to the NCAA announcement. Ohio’s eight Division I programs have yet to publicly weigh in on DeWine’s order. The measure has received support from Lt. Gov. Jim Tressel, a championship-winning former coach at Ohio State and Youngstown State. The state’s Division I ranks include No. 4 Ohio State of the Big Ten, Cincinnati of the Big 12 and six members of the Mid-American Conference. Under DeWine's order, public and private universities in Ohio would be able to allow the Class of ’22 athletes to play, even though the NCAA’s new guidance excludes those who have already played four seasons. The rule, passed in June, is the subject of multiple court fights. DeWine’s office declined to comment on the lawsuit. Although it is unusual for the NCAA to sue a governor, the organization has done so before. In the early 1990s, the NCAA prevailed in a case against then-Nevada Gov. Bob Miller over a state law that would have required the association to provide greater due-process protections during enforcement proceedings. COURT RULING OPENS DOOR FOR MICHIGAN TO ADD FORMER MIAMI, BOISE STATE PLAYER TO ROSTER MID-SEASON IN WILD MOVE In its court filing, the NCAA said it was trying "to halt a misguided attempt to give Ohio colleges and universities an unfair, unprecedented and unwarranted competitive advantage in stadiums and arenas throughout the country." "College sports, like all sports, depend on participants following the rules. (DeWine) is attempting to give Ohio institutions a hall pass to break the rules," the lawsuit says. The Ohio Supreme Court has already said it will determine the legality of the executive order. As part of that, it paused an appeals court ruling in a case there that had declared the ’22 athletes ineligible; the court asked both sides to file briefs in the case, in which basketball player Filip Borovićanin is the lead plaintiff, by next Monday. Baker said the NCAA did not believe the Supreme Court's order did, in fact, declare those players immediately eligible to compete. That case, like others around the country, is becoming more urgent by the day, as it involves football players, along with a handful of basketball players whose status for the upcoming season is in jeopardy. Among them: Gonzaga transfer Javon Bennett, Cincinnati's MJ Collins and Borovićanin himself, who played in an exhibition against Tennessee on Thursday night after DeWine's order put him back on the eligible list. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD For years, the NCAA has urged Congress to pass federal legislation that would curb lawsuits challenging its rules, which govern hundreds of thousands of athletes nationwide. The Senate has sent the Protect College Sports Act, aims to provide that protection, to the House, but its fate remains uncertain in an election year. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Nolan Lashley is Republic football's new touchdown king
articles.summary: Republic running back Nolan Lashley has shattered the single-season touchdown record. Lashley has scored 27 touchdowns through eight games.
articles.body:
REPUBLIC — If you lose concentration during a Republic football game, you've probably missed a Nolan Lashley touchdown.

The junior running back is finding the end zone early and often. Defenses can't slow him down, while his offensive line is generating holes big enough for an SUV to drive through.

No. 3 Republic (7-1) notched its biggest win of the season on Friday, Oct. 16, toppling Carthage 26-22 thanks to three rushing touchdowns from Lashley.

Lashley has now scored 27 touchdowns this season, breaking the school record for most touchdowns in a season. Jerney Jones held the previous record with 26 touchdowns in 2015.

Southwest Missouri has been a hotbed of great running backs. The best teams rely on their backs to win games. Republic is no different through Lashley.

Lashley has seen his peers' success around the region. It has only made him hungrier, he told the News-Leader last week.

"It makes me want to compete more," Lashley said. "When I go and look at stats, I see that I'm not leading in yards. It makes me want to compete. I want to be No. 1 in everything."

Lashley will forever be known as Republic's touchdown king. Head coach Ryan Cornelsen says his willingness to deliver hits and be fearless sets him apart from the rest.

"He takes a pounding, no doubt," Cornelsen said. "Running the ball in our offense is not for the faint of heart. He takes pride in that and does a good job."

The Tigers will face Willard (1-7) next week to close out the regular season. With expectations of a deep postseason run, Republic will continue to rely on Lashley.

The touchdown record will keep moving, just like Lashley's legs in every pile.

articles.title: “She hasn’t done this alone” – Linda Cohn Makes Brutal Angel Reese Claim as ‘Caitlin Clark Effect’ Comparisons Intensify
articles.summary: It’s been a while since the Angel Reese vs. Caitlin Clark narrative has commanded the spotlight.
articles.body:
It's been a while since the Angel Reese vs. Caitlin Clark narrative has commanded the spotlight. On Friday, WNBA analyst Linda Cohn reminded fans of this plotline.

In the latest edition of "The Linda Cohn Show," Cohn acknowledged Reese's rising prominence and said some fans were likening her popularity to Clark's.

"Angel Reese, as we all know, has become one of the biggest names in the WNBA. She's helping bring attention to the Atlanta Dream…Now, Atlanta has other outstanding players. She hasn't done this alone. Rhyne Howard, Jordin Canada, Allisha Gray, if she's healthy enough to play…Here's where I think the conversation is getting ahead of itself, and it's worth repeating. People are already trying to compare the Angel Reese effect with the Caitlin Clark effect."

According to Cohn, a genuine comparison can only be made by looking at the numbers drawn by the two WNBA All-Stars.

"Angel Reese absolutely has her own following and her own impact on the sport. But if we're gonna make comparisons about who's driving ticket sales, let's compare actual ticket sales. Let's compare attendance. Let's compare consistent demand over an entire season, not just a couple of Finals games."

Clark has downplayed suggestions of animosity toward Reese. She told off a reporter at the FIBA World Cup for asking whether she and Reese are "friends now."

"I'm Not Going to Shy Away From This Moment": Angel Reese Opens Up on Her Mindset Heading Into WNBA Finals

From the looks of it, Angel Reese isn't focused on a popularity contest, either.

On Friday's edition of "NBA Today," ESPN's Kendra Andrews shared some quotes from her conversation with the Dream star ahead of her first-ever WNBA Finals appearance.

"She said, 'To be a good player in the playoffs, you have to just elevate. You have to be someone who rises. The best players are the ones who are the greats, the ones that get the most respect, the ones that deliver on this level. I'm not going to shy away from this moment.'"

Reese is known to elevate her game in crunch situations, helping the LSU Tigers win the 2023 national championship. Now, her mettle will be tested again as the Dream take on the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals.

articles.title: Palisades defeats Hamilton in Western League showdown
articles.summary: Jameson Della Bella ran for 86 yards and two touchdowns while Robert Holohan ran for a touchdown and threw for one to lead the Dolphins to victory.
articles.body:
Jameson Della Bella ran for 86 yards and two touchdowns while Robert Holohan ran for a touchdown and threw for one more as Palisades dominated Hamilton 35-18 Friday night in a Western League showdown.

The Dolphins' defense was up to the task against Hamilton's highly touted quarterback Thaddeus Breaux, intercepting two of his passes and sacking him four times.

"It was fourth down, we had to make something happen, I saw him throw and I just ran full speed and dove for it," said safety Aidan Wilson-Turner, who picked off a pass over the middle at Palisades' 18-yard line to keep the Yankees off the scoreboard late in the first half.

Breaux, a sophomore who has received a scholarship offer from UCLA, threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns in last year's 46-30 loss to Palisades but was 27–of-44 passing for 217 yards Friday — most of that yardage in the fourth quarter with the outcome long decided. He threw scoring passes of eight, 11 and four yards.

"The defensive line did a great job putting pressure on him," Wilson-Turner added. "Our job in the secondary was to stay deep, playoff off them and stay true to our zones."

Palisades (4-3, 3-0) took a major step toward defending the league title with only games at fifth-place Fairfax and at home versus last-place Westchester remaining.

Hamilton, which fell to 3-5, 2-1, last won the league in 2014.

Della Bella's six-yard run gave Palisades a 21-0 lead midway through the second quarter and the Dolphins increased their advantage to 35-0 early in the third quarter on Holohan's 13-yard pass to Go Moriya and his four-yard quarterback keeper.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: PAC’s sudden death explained as official cause emerges weeks after AEW star’s passing
articles.summary: The official cause of death of AEW star PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, has been revealed weeks after his sudden passing at the age of 40. Accor...
articles.body:
The official cause of death of AEW star PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, has been revealed weeks after his sudden passing at the age of 40.

According to a report from the New York Post, the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office determined that the British wrestler died from bronchial asthma. His death was ruled natural.

PAC's passing shocked the wrestling world after he competed at AEW All Out in Chicago on September 26, with reports stating he was found unconscious in a rental car the following day.

Medical examiner confirms bronchial asthma caused PAC's death

A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office told the California Post that investigators had determined the cause of PAC's death following an investigation.

"Officials have determined what killed wrestling star Benjamin Satterley. A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office told the California Post on Monday that following a probe into his sudden death, investigators concluded Satterley — who performed in AEW rings as "Pac" — passed away from bronchial asthma.

"The manner of his death was officially ruled natural, the rep added. Satterley was discovered unconscious in a rental car outside of a CAVA in Des Plaines, Ill. at around 4 p.m. on Sept. 27."

The revelation offers an explanation for the sudden loss of a wrestler who remained active in the ring shortly before his death.

PAC had reportedly pulled over in a car park before being discovered unconscious. However, all the available reports do not provide further details about the medical emergency.

The wrestling world has continued to pay tribute to the former WWE star, who competed under the name Neville during his time with the company.

AEW held a tribute to honour PAC's life, while several of his peers also shared emotional memories of the wrestler. Names including Jon Moxley, Kevin Owens, Cody Rhodes and Bryan Danielson were among those reported to have spoken about his impact.

PAC built a reputation as one of wrestling's most exciting performers, known for his high-flying style and work across WWE and AEW.

His cause of death has now been officially established, but the loss continues to be felt by fans and colleagues who followed his career.

articles.title: “I Need Him to Get His Opportunity”: 5x Grammy Winner Sends Clear Message to Browns Over Shedeur Sanders
articles.summary: Lil Wayne wants the Cleveland Browns to have a quarterback headache, just not the kind that comes from another loss. The five-time Grammy winner would rather...
articles.body:
Lil Wayne wants the Cleveland Browns to have a quarterback headache, just not the kind that comes from another loss. The five-time Grammy winner would rather see the franchise wrestling with a difficult decision about Shedeur Sanders than reach the end of the season without knowing what Sanders can offer.

Speaking [on [Gridiron](]( co-hosted by Skip Bayless and Aqib Talib, during a conversation previewing the Packers-Cowboys matchup, Bayless asked Lil Wayne whether he wanted Sanders playing somewhere other than Cleveland.

"I need him to get his opportunity, and I think where he at he's going to get that opportunity," Wayne said on the show.

That distinction matters because Sanders is not currently Cleveland's starter. The Browns' official depth chart lists Deshaun Watson first and Sanders second, and the team has continued with Watson despite the attention surrounding him. Cleveland's decision to start Watson was made after evaluating the offseason, training camp, and preseason, rather than treating the competition as a week-to-week contest.

Head coach Todd Monken explained the decision in August, saying:

"We felt over the course of training camp and the offseason that (Watson) was ahead of Shedeur," Monken said. "Shedeur's closed that gap, for sure. And that's a credit to him. We look forward to Shedeur continuing to grow as a player, but ultimately, we're about Week 1. Putting our best foot forward over the next three weeks."

"Ultimately we expect him to play well or we wouldn't be starting him," he said.

Cleveland entered Week 6 with a 3-2 record after losing 17-12 to the New York Jets on October 11. Watson threw for 155 yards and was sacked eight times in that defeat, while a botched punt snap also hurt the Browns late in the game. The loss does not, by itself, mean Sanders should take over, but it gives the team another performance to evaluate as it weighs what it needs from its offense.

Watson has given Cleveland reasons to stick with him, but the numbers have hardly made the decision foolproof. Through five games, he has thrown for 1,010 yards and seven touchdowns with two interceptions, helping the Browns win three times. Then came the Jets game: just 155 passing yards, eight sacks, and a 17-12 loss.

Wayne, however, was not calling for Watson to be benched or suggesting Sanders had already earned the starting job. In fact, he made a point of saying he was happy to see Watson playing well earlier in the season.

"But I love to see Deshaun doing his thing now. I love that. I want Deshaun to give them a problem. I want them to actually have a problem at the end of this season, like, 'Man, what the hell do we do? What do we do? Why did we do this?' Well, I want them to, man. I want him. I like to see them smile."

Sanders has also been trying to make himself understood beyond the quarterback debate. In an interview with Cosmopolitan published October 8, he spoke about how he believes the public sees him.

"I wish people understood me more as a human being," he says. "I don't think a lot of people really know me. I'm just now starting to understand that. You hear a lot of things online, but every encounter I have in person, people end up saying, 'Oh, wow, he's actually a great guy.' Why would you think I'm a bad guy?"

The Browns may have their wins, but Wayne wants something far more entertaining: a quarterback dilemma Cleveland cannot simply shrug off. If Watson keeps the job, fine. But Wayne wants Sanders to make the decision uncomfortable, and that is where the fun begins.

articles.title: Pacers’ Tyrese Haliburton Caught Delivering NSFW Message to Bucks’ Ryan Rollins on Hot Mic
articles.summary: The Indiana Pacers and Milwaukee Bucks apparently have no plans to put their heated rivalry behind them. Pacers superstar Tyrese Haliburton made that perfect...
articles.body:
The Indiana Pacers and Milwaukee Bucks apparently have no plans to put their heated rivalry behind them. Pacers superstar Tyrese Haliburton made that perfectly clear Friday night when a confrontation with Bucks guard Ryan Rollins produced an NSFW exchange caught on a hot mic.

The incident occurred during Indiana's preseason finale against Milwaukee at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Oct. 16. Although the game carried little significance in the standings, neither player appeared interested in treating the matchup like a meaningless exhibition.

A video shared by PacersStatsMuse on X captured Haliburton repeatedly directing a profanity-laced insult toward Rollins. The exchange quickly attracted attention and offered another reminder that the tension between these Eastern Conference rivals remains alive.

Tyrese Haliburton's NSFW Message to Ryan Rollins Caught on Hot Mic

The confrontation began just 75 seconds into the opening quarter when Rollins shoved Haliburton from behind while the two players battled for rebounding position.

Officials called Rollins for a loose-ball foul, but the whistle did little to calm the situation. Haliburton immediately confronted the Milwaukee guard, delivering a message that required no interpretation.

"You a b**. You a b**, yeah you heard me, You a b****," Haliburton appeared to repeat toward Rollins.

Both players received technical fouls following the confrontation. However, Haliburton responded in perhaps the most effective way possible, knocking down a 3-pointer on Indiana's next possession. The moment was particularly noteworthy considering the circumstances surrounding Haliburton's return to basketball.

The Pacers star missed the previous season while recovering from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. Friday's matchup represented another opportunity to regain his rhythm before the regular season. Yet there was nothing cautious about his reaction to Rollins.

Haliburton showed the same competitive personality that has helped make him one of Indiana's most recognizable athletes. Even in preseason action, the All-Star guard clearly wasn't interested in allowing an opponent to push him around.

Pacers-Bucks Rivalry Shows No Signs of Cooling Down

The confrontation also highlighted the lingering tension between Indiana and Milwaukee, two teams that have developed considerable animosity through recent postseason battles.

The rivalry has featured physical play, heated exchanges and memorable moments involving players from both organizations. Friday's incident suggested those feelings haven't disappeared despite significant changes to Milwaukee's roster.

Former Pacers center Myles Turner also returned to Indianapolis wearing a Bucks uniform, adding another storyline to the matchup. Indiana fans greeted Turner with boos during introductions and whenever he touched the ball early in the game.

Meanwhile, Haliburton's performance offered Indiana something more encouraging than another viral confrontation.

The guard scored 17 points during the first half, adding six assists and three rebounds while shooting 7-for-14 from the field. His production continued a promising preseason stretch following an impressive outing against the Oklahoma City Thunder earlier in the week.

For Indiana, having Haliburton healthy and playing confidently remains considerably more important than anything said during a preseason argument. Still, the exchange with Rollins revealed something about the competitive atmosphere surrounding these teams.

The Pacers and Bucks will meet four times during the regular season, beginning Oct. 26 in Milwaukee. If Friday's confrontation was any indication, those meetings could feature considerably more than basketball.

articles.title: Watch Lakers’ Luka Doncic power through Nikola Jokic for tough and-1
articles.summary: Luka Doncic reminded everyone why he remains one of the NBA’s most difficult players to contain. He powered through Nikola Jokic for a tough and-1 in the Lo...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic reminded everyone why he remains one of the NBA's most difficult players to contain . He powered through Nikola Jokic for a tough and-1 in the Los Angeles Lakers ' preseason finale against the Denver Nuggets on Friday night. During the second quarter at Crypto.com Arena, Doncic attacked downhill and drove directly into the chest of the three-time MVP. Despite absorbing heavy contact from Denver's imposing center, the Lakers superstar maintained his balance, flipped a contested shot off the glass, and drew the foul to complete an emphatic three-point play .

The sequence offered a glimpse of Doncic's physical readiness heading into the 2026–27 campaign, even as Los Angeles fell 121-106. Doncic finished with 15 points, four rebounds, and three three-pointers in 19 minutes. He shot 4-of-8 from the field. Jokic countered with 17 points, six rebounds, and eight assists on 7-of-8 shooting. Meanwhile, Jamal Murray paced Denver with 21 points. Austin Reaves led the Lakers with 19 points. With the exhibition schedule complete, Los Angeles now turns its attention to Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Golden State Warriors.

Doncic has looked sharp throughout the 2026 preseason. He continues to be the centerpiece of head coach JJ Redick's offense while the Lakers carefully managed his minutes. Doncic opened the exhibition slate with 21 points against Sacramento before adding 23 in the rematch. He then capped his preparation with Friday's efficient performance against Denver. More importantly, his ability to create scoring opportunities through contact reinforced the physical edge that makes him such a difficult matchup. With Reaves providing another scoring option and Walker Kessler strengthening the interior, Doncic and the Lakers have plenty of reasons for optimism.

articles.title: High school football roundup: No. 1 Puyallup gets its revenge against Sumner
articles.summary: Scores, recaps, highlights and more from Week 7 high school football games around the South Sound.
articles.body:
Results, recaps, stats and more from Week 7 of the high school football season around the South Sound will be posted on this page Thursday, Friday and Saturday.

Puyallup has faced the state's most daunting schedule this season. First came a long bus ride east to face Rocky Mountain, one of Idaho's top programs. Then 3A state contender Bellevue in Week 2. Then a dramatic overtime matchup against reigning 4A state tournament runner-up Lake Stevens.

Check, check, check. Of all the marquee matchups and hurdles Puyallup has successfully cleared in 2026, though, the one Friday night just miles down the road probably meant a little more.

Puyallup outlasted valley rival Sumner in a back-and-forth contest, winning 36-34. Sumner bounced Puyallup in the 4A state tournament semifinals last year, handing the Vikings their only loss of the 2025 season.

So yes, Puyallup's players had this one circled on their calendars.

"Last year, they beat us in the semifinals, and we took that personal," said running back Malcolm Akuffo.

Akuffo ran for a pair of touchdowns. Puyallup quarterback Noah Smith connected with J'Isaiah Mitchell for two touchdowns.

Puyallup led 14-13 at half. Smith hit Mitchell for a 20-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter to push the led to nine points, but Sumner answered with an 11-yard run from Santos Hernandez-Ruiz. A 12-yard touchdown from run Akuffo put Puyallup back up by nine in the fourth quarter, but Sumner answered immediately with a 74-yard touchdown pass from Brennan Abbott to Gray Longoria.

Puyallup running back Logan Caldara scored next on a 51-yard run, then Sumner answered late when tight end Kai Moody fell on a loose ball in the end zone to pull the score within two. An onside kick was unsuccessful and Puyallup held on for the win.

"We've got a good group of guys," Puyallup quarterback Noah Smith said. "We've been working all off-season together. Coach Ross has a great team over there, so we knew they were going to fight back. So we've just got to just win that at the end of the day."

Akuffo ran tough in place of Briytan Bailey, who is sidelined with a knee injury. He's waiting on a second opinion to see if he'll be able to return to action this season. In the meantime, Akuffo is seeing more touches.

"Just trying to fill the role, you know?" he said.

Puyallup coach DJ Mims called Bailey and Akuffo "thunder and lightning." Now, Akuffo will have to find a way to be a little of both.

"He showed that tonight," Mims said. "He ran hard, he protected the football."

Sumner coach Keith Ross was thrilled with his team's effort and the way the offensive line pushed Puyallup around in the run-blocking game.

"I think that our kids learned tonight that they're still the real deal, and I'm really proud of them," he said. "We challenged them, you know? We've been kind of limping through games and our sense of urgency hasn't been there, and, you know, we're young, but tonight we proved to the whole state that we're a formidable foe."

Puyallup wraps up with a much-improved Emerald Ridge team next week before the league crossover championship game against Graham-Kapowsin, which will be another hurdle to clear. An undefeated run with wins over Lake Stevens, Bellevue, Sumner and Graham-Kapowsin will undoubtedly secure the No. 1 seed in the state tournament.

"Our league is tough, and then our non-league schedule is tough," Mims said. "And the biggest thing is just growth, dependability, trust, building that trust with our players and finding out, you know, who can and can't do what. And so you find that out in these games like this."

Lakes steamrolled Timberline on Friday night at Harry Lang Stadium, piling up 42 first-half points in a blowout win. Quarterback Elijah Gafa-Shields completed 6-of-10 passes for 132 yards and three touchdowns for the Lancers.

Lakes moves to 6-1 on the season and travels across the Narrows to Roy Anderson Field next week to face the Peninsula Seahawks for the 3A PSL Nisqually Division title.

Bethel bounced back with a comfortable win on Friday night against district rival Spanaway Lake.

Running back Deron Williams continued his breakout season, rushing for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries. Linebacker recruit Elu Feo had 10 tackles and two tackles for loss. Free safety Josh Panoy had a pair of interceptions for the Bison.

Bethel held Spanaway Lake to 181 yards of offense in the win.

"Our offense really executed well and controlled the clock," Bethel coach Travis Domser said. "Our defense got off the field and created turnovers. That's a winning formula for us. Spanaway Lake played super hard all night."

Curtis led 31-0 at half and never looked back, winning convincingly over the visiting Wolves on Friday night.

Quarterback Sam Patterson completed 12-of-16 passes for 280 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Receiver Taylor Smith had seven receptions for 117 yards and six carries for 52 yards and two rushing touchdowns.

"Super proud of our program and community on Homecoming weekend," Curtis coach Brian Jensen said.

Ever since the loss to Peninsula in the Fish Bowl, Gig Harbor has been rolling.

Max Schwab continued his impressive run of form, scoring one receiving touchdown, one rushing touchdown and snagging an interception on defense. Ian Sherer and Lucas Oliver added touchdowns. Quarterback Sawyer Hayes also scored on a QB sneak.

"This was senior night and all the seniors stepped up and played their heart out," Gig Harbor coach Jeff Scoma said. "We couldn't be prouder with our team and how they responded after week 3."

After last week's dramatic win over Tacoma rival Lincoln, this week was more of an exhale.

The game was never in doubt as the T-Birds cruised to a blowout win. KD Davis rushed for 101 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries, and caught three passes for 32 yards and a touchdown. DJ Morales rushed for 140 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries.

Defensive end Teaven Jones, one of the state's leading sack-getters a season ago, racked up six sacks in the win.

"After a big game last week we wanted to see our guys lock in and focus on tonight," Mount Tahoma coach Keith Terry said. "They did that. We wanted to be physical on both sides and start getting into a rhythm. We did that. It's been about our growth all season and we'll continue to focus on that."

A 40-yard Noah Collins field goal with 59 seconds left was the difference, sealing Stadium's three-point win over the Trojans.

Stadium quarterback Alec Richard passed for 240 yard sand a touchdown, and also rushed for two scores. Liam Clayton rushed for 115 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries. Receiver Xavion Sumlin caught five passes for 120 yards and a touchdown.

"Auburn kids played extremely hard and had a great offensive gameplan," Stadium coach Pat Johnson said. "Our kids showed resilience and toughness tonight and found a way to win a tough game in the fourth quarter. Our offense was the difference tonight. No turnovers and no punts saved us. We have a lot to clean up but anytime you can send kids to a homecoming dance winners, it's a good night."

Another week, another Tumwater blowout. This week, Aberdeen was the latest victim.

Tumwater racked up 428 yards of offense and led 48-0 at halftime before taking its foot off the gas.

Five Tumwater running backs (Tyler Briscoe, Grady Wall, Gavin Kaikkonen, Joey Haase and Cam Briscoe) scored touchdowns for the T-Birds. Senior quarterback Jake Reid made the most of his limited passing attempts, completing 3-of-3 passes for 107 yards and three touchdowns.

Defensively, Ethan Bello returned a fumble for a touchdown, while Grady Wall and Ethan Marson had sacks, a junior DL Finn Bracy had a tackle for loss.

"Pleased with the way our team executed in all phases today, in all grade levels," Tumwater coach Willie Garrow said. "The defense was outstanding, forcing multiple 3&Outs and giving the offense tremendous field position early in the game. The offense executed well, connecting on explosive plays to build a quick lead."

Graham-Kapowsin rushed for 427 yards and had 585 yards of total offense in a blowout win over the Tornados.

Quarterback AJ Tuivaiave completed 8-of-10 passes for 119 yards and two touchdowns.

The running backs feasted: Elijah Shanburn rushed for 143 yards and three touchdowns on six carries, Trejhaun Bell rushed for 107 yards and two touchdowns on seven carriesm Blake Pearson rushed for 88 yards on three carries and Romiece Taviuni rushed for 64 yards on three carries.

White River scored 49 of its 56 total points in the first half, running away with the 3A NPSL contest on Thursday night. Quarterback Chaz Strickland passed for five touchdowns in the first half, four of which went to No. 1 receiver Parker Fry. Logan Brame had a pair of rushing touchdowns.

Defensively, Chaz Blackie had a 93-yard pick six. Kicker Palmer Beus went 8-for-8 on PAT's and also had a touchdown reception.

Enumclaw found its rhythm in the second quarter, putting up 30 points in the period to extend its halftime lead to 44-0.

Junior running back Paxton Patterson had two touchdowns and had an interception on defense. Enumclaw moves to 6-0 on the season and should have another lopsided result next week with Kent-Meridian up next.

Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor, who is dealing with a turf toe injury , has been downgraded to doubtful and is not expected to play on Saturday against LSU, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel. The sophomore was listed as questionable on Wednesday and Thursday before his status changed Friday.

Taylor sustained the injury during the Bulldogs' September 26 win over Missouri and continued playing through the pain in the team's October 3 loss to Alabama. He eventually left the 56-23 defeat in the fourth quarter and was later seen wearing a boot on his right foot.

Through five games, Taylor has completed 102 of 154 passes, recording 1,450 passing yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed 43 times for 159 yards and a touchdown. His performances had placed him among the Heisman Trophy contenders before Mississippi State suffered its first loss of the season.

Redshirt freshman Puckett is listed as the No. 2 quarterback, while fifth-year senior AJ Swann and former Florida quarterback Jaden Rashada provide additional options.

Mississippi State could also be without its leading running back, Fluff Bothwell, who was downgraded to doubtful on Friday because of a lower-body injury. articles.title: Hockey legends back on the ice to mark anniversary
articles.summary: Swindon Wildcats are marking 40 years of ice hockey with a legends match featuring former players.
articles.body:
Ice hockey legends who have not skated in years are taking on the Swindon Wildcats team, to mark 40 years of ice hockey in the town.

The Wildcats, Wiltshire's only ice hockey team, was founded in 1986 by five players from the North East shortly after the opening of the town's Link Centre.

To mark the club's 40th anniversary, a team of former players are lacing up their skates again to face the current 2026/27 roster in a "one-of-a-kind" match on Saturday.

Steve Nell, managing director, said: "When I asked [the legends], everybody was: 'yes'. Now some of them are out there and it's a little bit tougher - [they're] stiff and haven't skated for a long time but everybody will be fine on the day."

The Wildcats play in the National Ice Hockey League (NIHL) and are the current reigning champions.

Nell said he was playing ice hockey in Sunderland when he and four others "got the opportunity" to move to Swindon in the 1980s and set up the team.

"There's not many clubs in the UK that have done 40 years," he said.

"The [players] have been a big part of the club over the years and there's still some people watching from the first year.

"It's such a big anniversary. I just think it's important to celebrate."

Daryl Lipsey, who was also one of the original founding players, said it had been years since he pulled on the kit but it was "nice to come back".

"The last time I played on the ice was 10 years ago, when we did the last legends game," he said.

For the anniversary match, he will not only be taking to the ice for the first time in a decade but going head-to-head with his two sons, who are on the Wildcats team.

"I just hope the fans aren't expecting me to be as good as I used to be," he said.

"But I'm looking forward to it. It will be fun."

Richard Howe, who played for the side in the 1980s and early 1990s, said it was going to "feel great" stepping out on to the ice in front of a packed Link Centre but he will "mainly be focussed" on staying on his feet.

"The first [training session] was pretty shaky - the second one was definitely better but I should be alright on Saturday," he said.

"I'm looking forward to getting back out in front of the crowd again.

"The hockey is probably of a higher standard but the crowd, the building, the changing room - it's all the same."

Lee Brathwaite, who started playing for the Wildcats in 1993 when he was just 14-years-old, said the club had experienced "some lean years" during its history.

"Certainly when I was playing we didn't have a huge amount of success," he said.

"But a club that stays around for 40 years is a pretty special thing."

Despite having been on the ice only twice since 2009, he said he is "absolutely buzzing and excited".

"My expectations for myself are quite low," he said.

"If I can get through without any major wipe outs, injuring myself or anybody else I'll be pretty happy."

articles.body:
The Boston Bruins are having a nice start to the 2026-27 season. Boston made some big offseason moves to maintain their status as a playoff team. On Friday night, they showed that they can stand tall against quality teams. Goalie Michael DiPietro was among the standouts in this contest.

The Boston netminder stopped 25 of the 27 shots he faced in this game. He received a huge offensive contribution at the other end of the ice, as well. In the end, the Bruins won 4-2, moving to 6-2-0 on the season.

DiPietro's win was notable as well. The 27-year-old won his first career NHL game. Furthermore, he became the second Bruins goalie in the last 48 years to win his first game at age 27 or older, according to NHL Public Relations. The other netminder to achieve that feat was Tim Thomas.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

DiPietro has had limited experience in the NHL prior to this season. In fact, this is the first time the 27-year-old has appeared in more than a single game in any one season. This was just the fourth career start for the former third-round pick.

The Bruins netminder was initially drafted by the Vancouver Canucks in 2017. He appeared in three games for them from 2018-19 to 2021-22. It wasn't until the 2025-26 campaign that he saw NHL action again.

DiPietro is now fully established as the Bruins backup goaltender. He will be the one stepping up when starting netminder Jeremy Swayman is getting a night off. So far, he has shown the ability to stand tall when his team needs him. It will be interesting to see how he builds on his performance in his next appearance.

articles.body:
Martin O'Neill reckons that Tony Bloom's ambition of winning the Scottish Premiership within ten years of his investment in Hearts is certainly a strong possibility, in fact the Celtic boss actually reckons it will happen…

Cameron Devlin of Heart of Midlothian reacts after conceding a third goal scored by Callum Osmand of Celtic (not pictured) during the Scottishl Premiership match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on May 16, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Of course it could – and probably would – have happened last season had it not been for Martin O'Neill returning to the club in early January after Celtic disastrous experiment under Wilfried Nancy , an appointment decision that more that anything else that exposes the Celtic board as charlatans.

16.05.2026 Celtic v Hearts, SPFL Premiership Callum Osmand goal against Hearts to give Celtic a 3-1 lead in the title decider. Photo Kenny Ramsay IMAGO/ News Licensing

"I do, yeah, I do. I think their recruitment is really good. I think that what they've done has put pressure on Celtic and Rangers. They're a definite challenge," the Celtic manager admitted.

"They kept going all last season. That was a big, big effort. They kept going and they took it right to the last couple of minutes. Are they capable of doing it? Yeah."

Celtic supporters at Celtic Park for the 2026 title showdown with Hearts. Celtic 3 Hearts 1. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Martin O'Neill added: "I think that they've got a certain system in place at this minute, which has been used down at Brighton. They used it there and they're scouring the European scene for these things.

"I thought in the opening game of the season against Aberdeen there might have been just a bit of a hangover from last season. I think they've put that to bed and I think they've come roaring back. I think they're capable of winning the league even before that."

Martin O'Neill, Manager of Celtic celebrates his teams third goal scored by Callum Osmand (not pictured) during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on May 16, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

"If you're looking at it from a neutral viewpoint I think it's only a great thing for Scottish football, that the O** F*** (sic) is being challenged in a big, big way. Rightly so. So it should be as well. Hearts have taken on that and I think they're here to stay.

"I have a lot of admiration for it. I really do. I have a great admiration for the way they stuck at it last season, the whole way through. Considering that they were up there all that time. You're up there, you're looking down, you feel as if 'oh gosh, could it happen'. They kept it going right to the end.

"Okay, so they've lost the manager and lost a couple of players as well. But I genuinely feel that they're a strong challenge. I think that can only be good."

Harry Milne of Heart of Midlothian speaks to a steward during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on May 16, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Asked if he expects a different kind of challenge from new Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken, Martin O'Neill said "No, I don't think so. I just think it's the essence of the club. They went so, so close. I think inevitably they were going to lose a couple of players.

"If you're thinking about the big centre-forward has gone to Rangers and things like that. But I think they've recruited really well and I just think they're physically very strong, again, which they were last season. And yeah, they are definitely challengers."

articles.summary: Manchester United Women have turned a corner lately after a rough start under new manager Eva Olid.The Catalan coach has guided her team to four consecutive...
articles.body:
Manchester United Women have turned a corner lately after a rough start under new manager Eva Olid.

The Catalan coach has guided her team to four consecutive wins, and they will look to make it five in a row when they face Charlton Athletic away on Sunday afternoon.

The BBC sat down with the United coach to pick her brains on the club's start to the new season.

Olid revealed that she has not had much time to explore the city, as she has been spending most of her time between the training ground and home while preparing for her new role.

Joining in the middle of pre-season was never going to be easy, but she explained what message she tried to convey to her players.

She stated, "I showed that I'm a person before a coach. I didn't have time to be aware of where I was. I just went there, be myself trying to transmit to the players how I see football, to work hard, that I'm going to be there for them, that I want to make them better players. Trying to transmit the key messages that I wanted the players to take from the first moment."

The Red Devils started the season in horrendous fashion, losing 1-2 to London City Lionesses before being taken apart 0-5 at home by Chelsea.

Nonetheless, Olid can see the positives from this hard week.

She asserted, "it was a difficult week. There were honest conversations. I took responsibility for a lot of things. I think that was a good starting point for the players. I was confident. It's crazy to say, I was confident because I knew what the problem was. And when you know the problem, you can change that."

The following week, United played excellently in a 1-1 draw versus Arsenal at the Emirates in a match they probably deserved to win.

Olid claimed she was incredibly happy with the team's performance and said, "when you are in Manchester United, you need to find a way to win. It's a challenge – how you can win and at the same time develop players and at the same time implement a new style of play. You need to find the balance of all that together. And I think these last weeks, we got to that point."

The new coach is settling into the city but has said that she still needs to find a "100% authentic" Spanish tapas bar in the city and hasn't been brave enough to try driving on British roads yet.

Finally, she explained how special it will be when she gets the chance to take her team to play at Old Trafford for the first time.

She added, "I came 13 years ago to a game – as a fan of football, and what I remember was amazing. On Saturday I went for second time and they showed me the changing rooms. The day that we play there this season, I will feel the happiest person in the world, like really like a dream."

articles.standfirst: Los vascos ganaron 2-0 a España en el Mundial de Pelota Vasca, que se disputa en Buenos Aires
articles.summary: Los vascos ganaron 2-0 a España en el Mundial de Pelota Vasca, que se disputa en Buenos Aires
articles.body: El equipo de Cesta Punta masculino de Euskadi venció este viernes por 2-0 a España en el Mundial de Pelota Vasca, que se disputa en Buenos Aires y tiene una subsede en la ciudad uruguaya de Colonia del Sacramento. El partido se disputó en el frontón de 54 metros del Real de San Carlos de esa ciudad, y marcó una jornada en la que fue reinaugurada la cancha ubicada en la histórica antigua plaza de toros. En el primer set, el equipo conformado por Xabi Barandika y Unai Lekerika dominó desde el comienzo y se impuso por 15-3 al integrado por Álex Hormaetxea y Gorka Mugartegui. El segundo comenzó más parejo y tuvo a Euskadi ganando, hasta que España logró igualar 8-8. No obstante, tras ese parcial, el conjunto vencedor recuperó su ventaja y cerró el duelo imponiéndose en el set por 15-12. Un día antes, en la primera jornada de competencia, el equipo femenino de Euskadi de paleta goma se impuso por 2-1 sobre España en el primer partido entre ambas selecciones absolutas. España enfrentará este sábado a Uruguay en xare y en paleta goma masculina, a Argentina en paleta goma femenina y a Francia en cesta punta individual femenina y masculina y en cesta punta femenina y masculina. Mientras tanto, Euskadi se medirá con México en cesta punta individual masculina y femenina, en cesta punta femenina y en frontball, con Francia en paleta goma masculina y con Argentina en parapelota. Los próximos duelos entre España y Euskadi serán el domingo 18 de octubre, cuando se enfrenten en xare, pala corta y cesta punta femenina. El XX Mundial de Pelota Vasca comenzó este jueves y se extenderá hasta el 24 de octubre con la novedad de la primera participación de Euskadi con un equipo propio en la máxima competición internacional de este deporte. La capital argentina ofrece tres sedes para la mayoría de las nueve disciplinas masculinas y femeninas del torneo, mientras que la subsede en Colonia del Sacramento está dedicada a los partidos de cesta punta. Las selecciones participantes son Francia, España, Euskadi, Portugal, Argentina, Uruguay, Estados Unidos, México, Cuba, Costa Rica, Venezuela, Perú, Brasil, Chile y Paraguay. El anterior campeonato del mundo se disputó en octubre de 2022 en Biarritz (Francia). España lideró el medallero con 20 preseas (nueve de oro, nueve de plata y dos de bronce), mientras que Francia fue segunda con 16 y México acabó tercero con diez metales. EFE scr/car

articles.title: Niceville wins district thriller over Crestview in Game of the Year
articles.summary: In a game that accounted for over 1,000 yards of offense and 83 points, Niceville escaped with a blocked extra point to move to 3-0 in District 1-5A.
articles.body:
Niceville beats Crestview in district thriller

CRESTVIEW — Signature win would be one way to describe it. A 3-0 unblemished record in District 1-5A would be another. Or, how about this, can we could just wax poetic about Georgia Tech commit Noah Renes looking like a Derrick Henry/Ray Lewis hybrid?

You can say what you want about Niceville amid a 4-4 start following an offseason filled with uncertainty and controversy, but simply put: The Eagles control their own playoff destiny.

And they do so by taking control back of a coveted rivalry Friday night, the Eagles walking into Jack Foster Stadium and delivering a 42-41 win for the ages over a Crestview team that could very well be 5-3 or 6-2 if had been at full health this year.

Noah Renes shined out of the heavy package with two touchdowns and a clutch 16-yard pickup on fourth down in the waning seconds, Deagan McCoy's go-ahead touchdown run with was one of three scores on a night he'd eclipse 300 yards and Niceville overcame a time-expiring Hail Mary between Zy Tassin and Jayden Goldsmith with a Renes block on the extra point to keep its postseason hopes well intact.

"I usually don't line up to block kicks," said Renes, who rushed five times for 26 yards. "But I was like, I might as well with the game on the line. I lined up in the C-gap, snuck up a little bit and I just jumped and I swatted it. I knew I blocked it right away."

"He does it all," McCoy said. "It shows his passion for the game, for Niceville football."

Pandemonium ensued. The student section rushed the field. And Adron Robinson was in tears afterward as his players embraced the first-year head coach, who in the offseason was promoted to turn around rivalries like this. Early setbacks to Mosley and Choctaw robbed him of that, and come Friday you saw an Eagle alum overwhelmed by the gravity of the win.

"Damn, we just kept fighting," Robinson said. "It wasn't always pretty, it wasn't always what we drew up, but all summer we talked about everything matters, and blocking the extra point matters. We got the win and we're 3-0 in districts, that's all that matters."

He's right. When Pace enters Eagle Stadium Wednesday, Nov. 4, a District 1-5A crown will be on the line. Niceville will have to find an answer for Makael Williams. And Pace will have to find an answer for Renes, McCoy, four-star tailback Jakobe Gilyard and a deep receiving core that includes White, Caleb Leonard, Jaxon Dark, Jason Leach and Austin Stanley.

Renes, who increased his touchdown total to six on the year, may demand a higher usage rate in the future.

"Heavy's back baby, heavy's back baby," Robinson said. "That's Niceville football."

The 16-yard run with a little over a minute to play on fourth down validated that.

"They were chopping at my legs, but I just kept going," Renes said. "I'm a big man. Good luck on bringing me down."

Two plays later, McCoy rolled out to his right, tucked it and dove head first for the end zone to put the Eagles up 42-35 after the extra point from Nate Martinez.

"It actually wasn't supposed to be a run play. It was a pass covered up," McCoy said. "I just kept my eyes downfield and was like, 'Why not?' I just went for it."

McCoy knew it'd be a dog fight. Zy Tassin showing out with four touchdowns, Manwell Robinson eclipsing the 200-yard rushing mark and Crestview topping 500 yards of offense affirmed that.

"We knew they were a lot better than their record, but we're always going to play Niceville football and do our best. This feels amazing to be 3-0 in districts. Pace is going to be fun."

Pace is 4-2 but just 1-0 in district with Tate, Navarre and Niceville looming.

"It feels great to be 3-0, but we can't get complacent with Pace coming to town Nov. 4," White said. "We just have to show up."

articles.title: Liverpool’s crazy £560k-per-week deals, now another £80m?
articles.summary: Liverpool went crazy on £560k-per-week deals. Now they look set to drop another £80m and we're struggling to make sense of it.Liverpool sparked a little bit...
articles.body:
Liverpool went crazy on £560k-per-week deals. Now they look set to drop another £80m and we're struggling to make sense of it.

Liverpool sparked a little bit of controversy this year with two deals that tallied around £560k per week. That was with their midfielder moves - renewing Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai to long-term contracts.

It was controversial if only because we're not sure the pair can play together in midfield. It also cast a spotlight on Alexis Mac Allister , who very much did not receive such a contract offer and went public on that fact.

The message here is that Liverpool view Gravenberch and Szoboszlai as the future of their midfield. That's really the only way to read contracts that approach £300k per week. At the same time, though, the Reds look set to purchase a new midfielder.

Sky Sports are one of several outlets claiming that Liverpool want Alex Scott. Bournemouth are open to a deal, too, as he's about to enter the final 18 months of his contract there.

But the Cherries want £80m. That's an awful lot of money for a midfielder that, given the massive contracts already handed out, Liverpool shouldn't really need.

However, they do need him. Or at least, Liverpool need a new midfielder who can bring a bit of control in the middle. It's why we've been big on the idea of signing Lamine Camara or Sergi Altimira.

Scott, though, does feel like he's cut from the same cloth as Gravenberch and Szoboszlai. Midfielders who can defend but would much rather push on towards goal and influence the attack.

And therein lies the problem. Scott is brilliant and homegrown and undoubtedly a player who could thrive at Liverpool. He just also feels like more of the same - a player who doesn't necessarily move the team on as much as he doubles down on a squad build that isn't really working.

So we're not entirely convinced about the plan here. Great player? Absolutely. The right one? Not so sure.

articles.title: Avalanche’s Jared Bednar makes sobering admission after Penguins win
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche have had a fantastic start to the 2026-27 NHL season. Colorado is looking to build upon its phenomenal 2025-26 regular season performa...
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche have had a fantastic start to the 2026-27 NHL season. Colorado is looking to build upon its phenomenal 2025-26 regular season performance. So far, they've picked up big wins. But head coach Jared Bednar is happy with simply winning.

The Avalanche came away with a big win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday. Colorado needed a rally after a bit of a sluggish start. After the game, Bednar made a tough admission regarding how the team has to continuously claw back into games .

"I'm convinced our guys know what makes us successful as a team, but we're just having a tough time right now putting together a full 60," Bednar said, via NHL.com. "But when we decide to play and play the right way with the right level of, for me it's intensity and discipline, then we're a really good team, and we're playing well. We just we have to find a way to just get it there for 60 minutes."

The Avalanche have not been able to string together wins as of late. As a matter of fact, they haven't strung together any consistent results. Colorado has alternated wins and losses in each of its last seven games, as NHL.com points out.

Colorado fell behind 2-0 in the first period, but was able to storm back after the opening frame. The Avalanche scored five unanswered goals to make it a 5-2 victory at the end of the night.

Colorado will need to find a way to start games on time with some consistency. They have a chance to win their second straight on Monday when they face the winless Philadelphia Flyers.

articles.title: “That’s my new nickname” – Angel Reese Embraces CJ McCollum’s Moniker While Praising Hawks Guard’s Support
articles.summary: A couple of days before the WNBA Finals, Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum praised Angel Reese for her impact on the Dream. McCollum even called Reese “the que...
articles.body:
A couple of days before the WNBA Finals, Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum praised Angel Reese for her impact on the Dream. McCollum even called Reese "the queen of the South."

In a media availability on Friday, Reese, a three-time WNBA All-Star, embraced the nickname.

"Shoutout to CJ McCollum. I appreciate the love and support, and I appreciate the support from the Hawks…I guess that's my new nickname, queen of the South. It's cool."

McCollum and Reese both came to Atlanta this year. In January, McCollum joined the Hawks via the trade that sent Trae Young to the Washington Wizards. Three months later, the Chicago Sky dealt Reese and a 2028 second-round draft swap to the Dream for two future first-round picks.

For both McCollum and Reese, the impact on winning was immediate. McCollum helped the Hawks reach the postseason after back-to-back seasons missing the playoff bus, while Reese (crowned 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year) has been integral to the Dream's unblemished playoff record heading into the Finals.

"She's Rebuilt Her Shot From Scratch": Dream Coach Karl Smesko Talks About Helping Angel Reese Fine-Tune Her Shooting

Angel Reese's first season with the Dream also marks Karl Smesko's second year as the team's coach. In a media availability on Friday, Smesko talked about spending time with Reese during practice sessions as she worked on her shooting.

"I thought it would be a good way for Angel and me to get to know each other a little bit and develop a relationship, if we could spend some time together every day…She's rebuilt her shot from scratch, from two weeks before the first game of the season, which is just remarkable that you'd even do that at that point."

While Reese isn't exactly known for her perimeter shooting, she has held her own from beyond the arc in the playoffs. When the Dream went 3-0 in the second round to eliminate the New York Liberty, Reese shot a combined 4-for-7 from deep.
