articles.title: Four Lakers players who did well in Friday's loss to the Nuggets
articles.summary: The Lakers got some solid performances from four players in their final preseason game on Friday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers ' 2026 preseason schedule is now in the books. They wrapped it up on Friday by hosting the Denver Nuggets at Crypto.com Arena, and once again, they weren't fully healthy. Guard Collin Sexton, who is expected to be a big contributor this season, missed the entire preseason with a leg injury, and forward Adou Thiero and guard Cameron Carr also didn't play.

The team looked disjointed, especially on offense early, and coach JJ Redick said it looked like his players weren't ready to play, at least from an energy standpoint. The Lakers committed many turnovers early as Denver regularly blitzed Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. They started to settle down in that department later, but they still trailed 62-55 at halftime.

They got to within 88-86 early in the fourth quarter, but as was the case in Tuesday's 101-89 loss to the Golden State Warriors, Redick went with a ragtag lineup down the stretch that consisted of fringe players such as Bronny James, Dalton Knecht and Chris Mañon. The Lakers fell behind by a sizable margin and couldn't make up ground, resulting in a 121-106 loss.

Still, four players performed relatively well and seem to be ready and prepared for the team's regular-season opener on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

Williams, a 6-foot-9 forward the Lakers signed to a minimum contract during the summer, missed their last three games. But he returned on Friday and made a definite contribution.

He scored 14 points and made all but one of his six field-goal attempts while hitting both of his 3-point tries. Outside shooting has been a weak link for him -- he made just 34.3% of his 3-point attempts, which was a career high, last season. But in his two exhibition games this month, there have been indications that perhaps he's turning the corner in that department.

Mamukelashvili has looked every bit as good as advertised -- and then some -- throughout the preseason. He has appeared in each preseason game, and on Friday, he was impactful.

He finished with 15 points on 5-of-10 overall shooting and 3-of-7 from downtown, eight rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in just 21 minutes. He did a good job of contributing to L.A.'s transition game by getting a couple of fast-break dunks and pushing the ball off defensive rebounds.

The big man is poised to be a major part of the team's success.

The two-way wing came off the bench on Friday, but he still played 28 minutes and dropped 11 points while making half of his six 3-point attempts. He also added three assists without committing a single turnover.

His shot selection and decision-making off the dribble can be a bit loose and questionable at times. But he has the ability to give the Lakers a lift on both ends of the floor.

Hardy went 5-of-9 from the field and 3-of-5 from 3-point land, giving him 13 points in just 14 minutes. He has always been a dependable 3-point shooter, and even though most of the rest of his game is generally flawed, he appears capable of giving the Lakers serviceable minutes in a pinch, especially if they lose at least one of their main ball-handlers to injury.

articles.title: Pumas grabs a key victory after defeating Atlante
articles.summary: Pumas defeated Atlante by a 2-1 score and got their first victory since September 10th.
articles.body:
Pumas got back to the victorious road after defeating Atlante by a 2-1 score. In a lively match, Pumas overcome some defensive mistakes to get victory in more than a month and temporarily climb to 9th place in the Liga MX standings. Pumas will travel north for their Wednesday clash against Santos Laguna in Torreon while Atlante will travel even further north as they face off against FC Juarez.

The 1st half started with Pumas coming out with Alan Medina taking the place of suspended Cesar Huerta. A great cross into the area from Eugenio Pizzuto was just cleared by Pablo Bennevendo before Eduardo Tercero could have had a close range header. A cross into the area would be cleared into the path of Jhojan Julio, who got off a right footed shot that forced a good save from Pumas' goalkeeper, Keylor Navas. Rodrigo Lopez got off a right footed shot from way outside the area that went well wide. A great thru pass from Adalberto Carrasaquilla would get to Uriel Antuna, who got off a bad left footed shot that went wide, wasting a great opportunity. Luis Calzadilla got into the area and got off a right footed shot that went wide. A great run by Luis Puente ended with the ball getting to Julio, who got off a right footed that was brilliantly saved by Navas. Because of protesting, the referee would give a red card to Atlante's coach, Miguel Herrera. A cross into the area was headed by Robert Morales into the path of Juninho, who volleyed the ball from close range past Atlante's goalkeeper, Oscar Jimenez to score and give Pumas the 1-0 lead. A couple of minutes later, Luis Calzadilla was given time and space to get off a right footed shot in the area that went past Navas to score and tie the match at 1-1. Calzadilla would get off a right footed shot from outside the area that Navas would make another great save off. The 1st half ended as the match was tied in a very lively match.

The 2nd half started with neither team making a change so far. Pizzzuto got off a great left footed shot from outside the area that forced another save from Navas. Off a counter, the ball got to Antuna, whose right footed s hot was well saved by Jimenez. Pumas subbed out Alan Medina for Victor Arteaga. A cross into the area was headed well wide by Julio. Atlante subbed out Edgar Jimenez for Diogo Bagui. Off a counter, a great run from Carrasquilla ended with a wonderful pass to Juninho, who got off a left footed shot past Jimenez to score and give Pumas the 2-1 lead. Atlante subbed out Aaron Quiros for Christian Bermudez. A cross into the area was deflected into the path of Pedro Vite, who whiffed on his volley and wasted a chance. A cross into the area was deflected terribly by Ruben Duarte, forcing Navas to make a great save to prevent the own goal. Pumas subbed out Juninho for Alvaro Angulo. Atlante subbed out Eugenio Pizzuto and Eduardo Tercero for Joaquin Moxica and Jairon Charcopa. A longball looked like a good chance for Morales but Jimenez was able to clear the ball before he had a 1 vs 1 chance. Pumas subbed out Uriel Antuna for Santiago Lopez. The time ended and Pumas got a very important result to get back to their winning ways.

Pumas got a key victory after defeating Atlante on Friday night. The return of the clash between Mexico City teams had Pumas being at times lucky as although they had a lot of the possession, their defensive mistakes meant that Atlante had a lot of opportunities that goalkeeper Navas prevented from going to the scoreboard. Pumas showed some life at offense, something they had already done in their 3-3 tie on Sunday against Cruz Azul. A couple of dangerous counters by Carrasquilla showed that Pumas is bouncing back on offense but the same can't be said about defense. Pumas will have another road match midweek when they travel north to face the fast improving Santos. Atlante will also go north as they play their first ever Liga MX match against FC Juarez in Ciudad Juarez on Tuesday.

articles.title: Chelsea fans’ preferred lineup against Everton: Never change a winning lineup
articles.summary: Everton vs. Chelsea, Premier League: Preferred lineup
articles.body:
It's the age-old question. Do you change a winning lineup? Do you play to your strengths as you perceive them, or do you try to anticipate and react to the opponents' perceived strengths? The answers to those two questions rarely align exactly.

As far as the WAGNH Community's concerned, the correct answer is to stay with what worked last week and what gave us our best performance yet of the young season. This means the midfield pairing of Moisés Caicedo and Jordan Henderson, and the back three of Levi Colwill, Maxence Lacroix, and Josh Acheampong. There should be no doubt about the front-three of course.

In fact, it's only at right wing-back where we get a bit of indecision, but a converted Pedro Neto (55%) still holds off the presumed first-choice in Marco Palestra (41%). The summer signing had impressed in preseason but has been hurt ever since. He did come off the bench last week to make his debut, so presumably his first start for Chelsea isn't too far behind … but maybe not just yet.

articles.title: How to Watch: Kansas at K-State
articles.summary: The bad thing about long winning streaks is that they might end.
articles.body:
Twice in the last three years, the streak appeared to be in jeopardy. Last season, it wasn't even close. Today, K-State will try and extend their winning streak over Kansas to "voting age".

The Kansas State Wildcats (3-2, 0-2 Big 12) host the Kansas Jayhawks (2-3, 0-2 Big 12).

Kansas leads the all-time series 64-54-5, although officially it's 63-55-5 because of cheating. Kansas has decided that the Big 8 ruling declaring their 1980 win a forfeit doesn't matter anymore since there's no Big 8 anymore. Go figure.

But it's been 17 in a row for the Cats since a three-game KU winning streak in the late 00s. Obviously there's a lot at stake today, not least the opportunity to avoid an 0-3 start in conference play. It's a big game.

Kansas hasn't really been competitive against opponents with pulses, but K-State hasn't really either so there's another reason for trepidation.

Saturday, October 17, 11:00am CT at Bill Snyder Family Stadium (50,000) in Manhattan, Kansas.

The game is officially a sellout, with standing-room only tickets avaliable from the ticket office. Via third-party outlets, you're not getting in the door for under $78 at this writing, and the median price is $122.

The good news: the sun will be out, and game-time temps will start in the low 50s anr rise to nearly 60 by game's end. The bad news? It'll probably be under 40° when you start your tailgate. Bundle up.

Per our friends at DraftKings K-State is a 3.5-point favorite with a 55.5 over. That should translate to a 30-26 K-State win. The money line is -175 for the Cats, +145 for the Jayhawks.

FS1 with Eric Collins and Spencer Tillman.

As always, Wyatt Thompson, Stan Weber, and Matt Walters will be on hand on the K-State Sports Network as well as via satellite on SiriusXM 173 or 237.

The game will stream on FOX Sports (cable, satellite, or internet tv subscription required). Audio available via kstatesports.com . Live stats provided by StatBroadcast .
